To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

activation of metabotropic glutamate receptors in retinal amacrinne cells enhances the function of postsynaptic GABA receptors, and that this effect depends on elevations in intracellular Ca2+ and protein kinase C activity.

activation of metabotropic glutamate receptors on GABAergic amacrinic cells can enhance currents through GAB AA receptors, and that these enhancements are dependent upon elevations of cytosolic calcium and activation of protein kinases.

activation of group I metabotropic glutamate receptors in retinal GABAergic amacrinne cells leads to activation of PKC and enhancement of GABAA receptor-mediated currents. 1Supported by NIH EY 015473.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of GABAergic amacnine cells in retinal signal transduction, and how the function of these cells is modulated by glutamate from bipolar cells.
the role of metabotropic glutamate receptors and other second messenger pathways in modulating synaptic function in the retina.
the mechanisms that underlie the modulation of synaptic function in retinal interneurons and the role that these mechanisms play in retinal information processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glutamate from bipolar cells can regulate the function of GABAergic amacrinic synapses in retinal circuits through multiple mechanisms.
the GABAergic amacrinic cells express metabotropic receptor, mGluR-5, which is linked to the IP-3 pathway and when activated by glutamate, can stimulate temporalsy diverse Ca2+ elevation.
mGluR-mediated Ca2+ signaling is a key mechanism for regulating GABAergic transmission in the retina.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

glutamate from the presynaptic bipolar cell can work through multiple mechanisms, including activation of GABAA receptors, mGluR-mediated enhancement of GABAA receptor function, and NO-dependent enhancement of GAB AA receptor function, to modulate GABAergic amacrineto-amacrine cell synapses. 1Supported by the NIH.
glutamate can modulate the activity of amacrine cell GABA receptors via two distinct pathways: the IP3 pathway and the NO pathway.

glutamate released from bipolar cells can regulate amacrine cells through a combination of direct and indirect mechanisms, including activation of ionotropic glutamate receptors, mGluR-dependent Ca2+ elevating and PKC activation, and Ca2+-dependent NO release.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glutamate can act as a modulator in the retina, and that the consequences of glutamate activation are dependent on the cell types that are contacted.
glutamate released from bipolar cells is a potent neuromodulator of retinal amacrine cell signaling.
glutamatergic signaling can modulate the function of GABAergic synapse in the retina.
